learning_rate_assignment_policy: start IDs 1-8 receive alpha in [0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.35,0.5,0.7,0.9] respectively, identical to M1_stimulus_kernel_v1's own eight learning rates, spanning near-frozen (slow-integrating) to near-instantaneous (fast, noisy-tracking) history kernels; a=logit(alpha)
note: Extended_WSLS has no sensory coordinate (no w/s0/kappa), so only M0's own ell_short/ell_long columns are reused here, unchanged, by start_id, each paired with one distinct learning-rate logit -- the same eight rows and the same eight learning rates M1_stimulus_kernel_v1 already uses, identical in spirit to how m1_hmm_true_v1's own initialization table pairs those same eight rows with eight varied hazards. This is a deliberate eight-point joint design for multi-start coverage, not a controlled one-parameter-at-a-time identifiability sweep (see M0's own initialization table note) -- lapse and learning rate are intentionally varied together across the eight starts, not crossed independently.
